Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with characteristic concentric rings ('bullseye' target pattern) starting on older lower foliage, surrounded by chlorotic yellow halos.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis or copper octanoate spray. Strip affected lower leaves immediately and mulch soil to prevent fungal spore splash.
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Foliar application of Chlorothalonil (0.2%) or Mancozeb (0.25%) at 7 to 10 day intervals during warm humid weather.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Maintain 3-year Solanaceous crop rotation, utilize drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers, and ensure optimal plant spacing (60 cm) for canopy airflow.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions on leaves and stems, often accompanied by white fluffy fungal mycelium on leaf undersides in high humidity.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) or copper hydroxide sprays applied as early protectants; remove and incinerate severely infected vines.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Systemic fungicides such as Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) or Cymoxanil; spray proactively when night temps are 10-15C and relative humidity exceeds 90%.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free transplants, eliminate cull piles and volunteer tomato/potato plants, and monitor local late blight weather alerts.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant uniform dark-green compound leaves, robust venation, absence of lesions, spots, or chlorosis.
Tomato___healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain balanced vermicompost tea or seaweed foliar spray every 2 weeks for systemic acquired resistance.
Tomato___healthy.chemical_treatment: No chemical intervention needed. Avoid unnecessary prophylactic fungicide applications.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Continue regular nutrient management (NPK 4:2:4 during vegetative, 2:1:4 during fruiting), optimal soil moisture, and pest scouting.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Small brown angular spots enlarging to show concentric dark rings, restricted by leaf veins; premature leaf defoliation.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Spray neem seed kernel extract (5%) or copper oxychloride; remove infected leaf trash post-harvest.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin, Difenoconazole, or Chlorothalonil every 10-14 days.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertilization; stressed plants are significantly more susceptible.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding dark brown to purplish-black water-soaked lesions on leaf tips and margins; white downy mildew on undersides.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Fixed copper fungicides before infection sets in; destroy infected plants immediately.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Dimethomorph, Cymoxanil, or Propamocarb hydrochloride sprays upon first symptom detection.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars, avoid overhead watering, hill tubers well to prevent spore wash into soil.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green leaves, undamaged petioles, vigorous vegetative canopy.
Potato___healthy.organic_treatment: Apply bio-fertilizer and foliar micronutrient spray to maintain vigorous canopy.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil hilling, scouting schedule, and optimal soil drainage.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Elongated cinnamon-brown to golden powdery pustules (uredinia) scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_treatment: Sulfur-based dusts or bio-formulations of Trichoderma harzianum; early crop scouting.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_treatment: Foliar triazole or strobilurin fungicides (e.g., Pyraclostrobin, Propiconazole) if pustules appear before tasseling.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids; early planting to avoid peak airborne urediniospore dispersal.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Dull olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves, turning dark brown with distinct margins; leaf puckering and early leaf drop.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_treatment: Liquid lime sulfur or potassium bicarbonate sprays during early green tip and petal fall stages.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil, Captan, or Difenoconazole applied during primary infection periods (spring rains).
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and shred or compost fallen autumn leaves to eliminate overwintering pseudothecia; prune trees for open sunlight.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, circular, water-soaked dark spots that develop into irregular lesions with necrotic centers and yellow halos; blossom drop.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Copper hydroxide mixed with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens; avoid working in fields when foliage is wet.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper bactericides combined with Mancozeb (to overcome copper resistance in Xanthomonas strains).
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified hot-water treated pathogen-free seeds; eliminate solanaceous weed hosts.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves, strong erect branching, intact leaf lamina without chlorosis or necrosis.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.organic_treatment: Foliar application of fish emulsion and seaweed extract.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil moisture consistency to prevent blossom end rot and foliar stress.
